subject: Procurement: PO pre-authorizations, credit holdbacks, and invoice cadence
messages:
From: Jenna Smith <jenna.smith@neptune-health.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Cc: procure@neptune-health.com
Date: 2026-08-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: PO fields, net terms and credit holdback question

Vanessa — thanks for the demo yesterday. Procurement ran the proposed commercials past our AP team and we have three blocking items before we can issue a PO: 1) our ERP requires a specific PO header (entity id, BU code, tax treatment flag), 2) our standard net terms are Net45 (we can stretch to Net60 with an approved prepayment or credit holdback), and 3) we prefer monthly consolidated invoices rather than per-delivery invoices.

Two quick asks: can Redwood accept a PO with a 10% holdback until quarterly reconciliation (so we can keep Net60), and can you provide a PO template and an invoice cadence proposal that maps to our monthly consolidated statement? I attached our procurement checklist for reference.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

— Jenna Smith
Senior Procurement Manager
Neptune Health
procure@neptune-health.com
(415) 555-0183

Attachment: Neptune_Procurement_Checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Jenna Smith <jenna.smith@neptune-health.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom@redwood.ai>, tessa_morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-16T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PO fields, net terms and credit holdback question

Jenna — appreciate the clear summary and the checklist. High-level response: yes, we can accept a PO with your ERP fields included and support monthly consolidated invoices. On terms/holdback there are two standard approaches we offer depending on the customer's accounting preference:

- Option A (preferred for revenue recognition): Net45 + 0% holdback; Redwood offers a 3% prepayment discount if Neptune can prepay 30 days of committed spend.
- Option B (procurement-friendly): Net60 with 10% quarterly holdback — Redwood will agree milestone reconciliation to release the holdback after invoice validation and service acceptance.

I attached our PO template populated with the common PO header fields your ERP requires, plus two suggested invoice schedules (monthly consolidated and monthly consolidated with 10% reserve). Ben — can you confirm how this impacts the price ladder/discount band? Priyom — if Neptune wants to go Option B, we should note a small margin impact; I think a 50–75 bps concession to the effective rate covers the holdback risk.

If helpful, I can join procurement's call Thursday.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.ai
Attachment: Redwood_PO_Template.pdf (PDF stub); Neptune-SOW-v1.docx (docx stub)

From: ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jenna Smith <jenna.smith@neptune-health.com>, tessa_morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-17T08:29:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PO fields, net terms and credit holdback question

Vanessa / team — quick pricing note: Option B (Net60 + 10% holdback) increases our working capital exposure. To keep ARR/tier intact while covering risk, we can offer: a) the currently proposed tiered volume discount schedule, minus a 0.5% absolute reduction on list price (so effective concession ~50 bps), or b) keep pricing intact and request a quarterly reconciliation SLA (7 business days) to release holdback faster.

I'm OK with either; recommend offering Neptune the choice in writing. If they want the deeper concession we may need an updated commitment window (12 months).

— Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Revenue Operations
ben@redwood.ai

Thanks — this is helpful. Procurement prefers Option B operationally (Net60 + 10% holdback) because it aligns with our payment runway. A couple of clarifications before we sign: 1) can Redwood commit to releasing the holdback within 10 business days of receipt of Neptune's quarterly reconciliation materials? 2) if we accept the 0.5% pricing reduction, what's the minimum term/commitment you need to lock that rate?

We also need the PO header to include a line for the Neptune entity tax ID (we'll supply offline). We plan to issue a PO on Friday pending your confirmation on timing and term.

— Jenna

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: PO fields, net terms and credit holdback question

Jenna — we can do that. Final confirmation below for your PO team: 

- PO fields: Redwood will accept Neptune-specific header fields (entity id, business unit code, tax ID, tax treatment flag). Please add the tax ID on the PO line item as discussed.
- Invoice cadence: monthly consolidated statement with line-level activity and a single monthly invoice PDF.
- Payment terms: Net60 with a 10% quarterly holdback. Redwood will release holdback within 10 business days of receipt of Neptune's reconciliation packet (detailed CSV + acceptance sign-off).
- Pricing concession: 0.5% absolute reduction on list price in exchange for a 12-month committed term; Redwood will honor previous quoted tiering for volume bands.

If that matches your procurement team's needs, we'll expect PO issuance today and will attach an amended SOW and execution-ready order form once we receive the PO and tax ID. Happy to join your Friday call for sign-off — Vanessa (me) and Priyom can be available at 2pm PT.

Best,
